items.stem: A document database stores each student's enrollments, with the course titles copied inside each student's document. Which question is hardest for it to answer?

options.text: Which students are enrolled in MGT 45?
options.feedback: The data is organized by student, so the database must scan every student's document or maintain a second index by course.
The documents were organized for this question. One read returns the schedule.

options.text: What is the name of this student?
options.feedback: The name is stored in the same document. One read returns it.

options.text: How many courses does this student take?
options.feedback: The list in the student's document can be counted in one read.

items.stem: A teammate misspells a field name when saving one student's document in a document database. What happens?

options.text: It stores the misspelled name as a new field and raises no error.
options.feedback: Documents in the same collection can have different fields, so your application code must enforce the schema.

options.text: The database rejects the document because the field name is unknown.
options.feedback: Rejection is what a relational database does with data that does not fit its columns. A document database accepts it.

options.text: It corrects the spelling automatically from the other documents.
options.feedback: A database does not guess what a field name should be.

options.text: It deletes the older version of the document and keeps the new one.
options.feedback: Saving a document replaces or updates it. A new field name does not trigger deletion.

items.stem: Your {{project}} team is not sure which questions the app will need to answer. Which choice is the safer start?

options.text: A relational database, because new questions need only filters and joins.
options.feedback: Rows suit questions you did not plan for, and a relational schema is easier to fix when it was wrong.

options.text: A document database, because it is faster for every kind of question.
options.feedback: A document database is faster for one known question. At student project data volumes you will not notice a difference.

options.text: A key-value store, because it is the simplest kind to set up.
options.feedback: A key-value store has no structure for asking new questions, so it is the hardest to change later.

options.text: A graph database, because everything in a business is connected.
options.feedback: A graph database suits questions about multi-step connections. Most student projects need ordinary filtering and joins.
